title: Melromarc’s Tightrope Walk
text: “What’s that? Did something happen?”
At this point, Ren showed up bringing along Rafumi, Keel, and Luna-chan. Wolf shifted into his wolf-man form to match the puzzled Keel.
“Oh, so it was Wolf. I’d heard something about him, and now he’s back, huh.”
“Ohh! Wolf-bro’s back!”
“The much-changed Sword Hero, and Keel… ah, so he’s regained his sense of self. I look forward to working with you all going forward.”
At Wolf’s reply, both Ren and Keel wore matching expressions of shock.
“Cute ones… they’re surprised…”
Luna-chan looked utterly entranced by the faces Ren and Keel were making.
“Whoa! You can talk now, Wolf-bro! I’m Keel! Nice to meet ya!”
Ren watched the exchange unfold with a wary look.
“Hmm… so this is the new Claw Hero. Come to think of it, this is one I recognize from this loop.”
“Vof.”
Wolf seemed wary of Rafumi in turn.
“What’s with that attitude?”
“He’s probably just wary of your insufferably arrogant attitude, that’s all.”
When Ren scolded Rafumi, Rafumi looked at Wolf with an expression that said none of this concerned him in the slightest.
“Well, I suppose a world like this can exist too. Be grateful for the encounter, I say.”
“Ah.”
“You’re not in the data, so I’ll observe you for a while. If you seem useful, I’ll consider it going forward.”
Wolf’s ears twitched sharply.
“Hey, bro! Now that Wolf-bro can talk properly, does that mean he’s gonna join the circus acts? What’s he gonna do? Same as before?”
“Since he can hold a proper conversation now, if he’s willing to perform, we’ll have him join in.”
“Ohh! Awesome! I wanna be in one too! Not just dancing in the background!”

Keel and the others were, as always, making a fuss about wanting to be in the circus, indeed. Big Sister and Big Sister’s friend were the same way. Well, they did get to participate somewhat on the Zeltoble side. It seemed like being allowed to perform on the Melromarc side was regarded as something like making the first string.
“Everyone’s been working hard, so the acts keep increasing, and the competition’s getting fiercer…”

By the way, apparently Panda and the others had become quite popular in the Melromarc-side acts. As they say, versatility helps even a Demi-Human Beastman get by. Apparently they were being praised even without doing an abuse show. Father’s slave-abuse show had also become a regular fixture, though its popularity was said to be middling. Incidentally, up on the circus net at present, Lazy Pig was, as always, sleeping. Lately wasn’t it looking less like work and more like it was just up there napping all the time?
“Bwoink…”
Lazy Pig fluttered a piece of paper down from the net toward Father. Father picked it up and knit his brows in a troubled expression.
“Um, let’s see, apparently Elena-san’s already negotiated with the slave trader and gotten permission for an act Keel-kun and the others can join. Want to give it a try, Keel-kun?”
“Eh!? For real!? I can really be in it!?”
“Yep, you can be in it. Ren’ll be joining too, though.”
“Why do I have to do it too!”

Ren had, at some point, taken to coming in and out of the circus tent, indeed. Since Rafumi was doing the body-double work and handling hero duties with the others in his stead, Ren had nowhere in particular to be, and so was bored, presumably.
“Well, if Ren doesn’t want to, I guess there’s nothing to be done — I mean, it is a pretty brutal act…”
“The only reason I’m even here in the first place is because no matter where I go to rest, Luna drags me back here and I can’t escape! Naofumi! Do you get that!”
Luna-chan had taken a liking to Ren and would carry him back whenever she found him sleeping somewhere. Lucky you, Ren — at least you’re not alone anymore, I say.
“C’mon, sword-bro, it’ll be great! Let’s do it together. I bet it’ll be fun.”
“Hmph! I have zero interest in the circus.”
“But bro, you’ve done so much for us — you even made us a tasty meal today, right? Isn’t it about time you did something to pay us back?”
“Ugh…”

Ren was being worn down by Keel’s sparkling-eyed persistence. Incidentally, Luna-chan was watching this exchange between Ren and Keel with equally sparkling eyes. She looked thoroughly delighted, indeed.
“Ugh, fine… I’ll do it, all right? I’ll do it.”
“Are you really sure? Don’t come crying to me later if you get mad or regret it, okay?”
“If I don’t do it, this brat won’t shut up. Try being on the receiving end of those eyes for once.”
“Well, if Ren’s okay with it, then I guess it’s fine…”
Half out of resignation, Ren caved to Keel’s pushing and ended up agreeing to participate.
“Ho… I see, so this is the act… Well, I suppose it’s fine, if it means Keel and Luna get to enjoy themselves?”
Rafumi, too, seemed to have grasped the contents of the act by this point. No issues there, indeed.
And so, the time came for today’s act, in which Keel and Ren would take center stage.
“Oi! What is the meaning of this!”
“Sword-bro, hurry up and go on ahead!”
What was happening was this: an act in which Keel and Ren would tightrope-walk across a rope set up high above the circus grounds.

“Behold, this day’s Tightrope of Death! Down below, a gluttonous giant bird waits with mouth agape, eager for the wretched, wicked dog-beast Beastmen to fall! Will today’s sacrifices make it across the rope, or will they plummet down to become its feast? Do stay tuned!”

With that sort of announcement, Keel and Ren — who knew absolutely nothing about any of this — were hoisted up to the heights and made to cross the rope with zero rehearsal, indeed. And down below, waiting eagerly for Ren and Keel to fall, was none other than Luna-chan.
“Kweh! Kweh—!”

In her Filolial form, mouth open wide, her job was to catch Keel and Ren as they fell. Since Luna-chan adored Ren and Keel so dearly, the plan was for them not to actually be eaten, but simply “taken home” as it were. Upon falling, smoke would be set off so they’d land safely tucked within her feathers. Of course, since they were being forced across against their will, my job was to walk behind them, poking them along with my spear.
“Spear-bro, quit poking! Whoa! It’s shaking! I’m falling!”
“Oi, Motoyasu, cut it out! Damn it! Stop pushing! S-somebody!”
Poking and prodding Keel and Ren along, I advanced steadily across the taut rope.
“Ohh dear, at this rate today’s sacrifices might just escape with their lives! How dreadfully uninteresting! Everyone! Let us bring down the hammer of judgment upon these wretched Beastmen!”
With that cry, the rope was made to shake violently. On top of that, the audience began hurling all manner of things — stones for sabotage among them.
“Oi! Cut it out!”
“Stop shaking it! What are you people throwing?! Argh!”

Keel and Ren, each deflecting the projectiles with sword or hand, pressed onward regardless — though the shaking made for quite the ordeal. As for me? With my chi manipulation and sense of balance, crossing a tightrope was child’s play, indeed. Now then, time to fall!
“Ngh… like hell I’ll fall!”

With a burst of speed, Ren tried using the rope itself as a springboard to dash across. Not so fast! I let loose a small, downscaled Air Strike Javelin laced with an extra paralysis effect, and gave Ren a little poke with it.
“Guh—!”
Ren lost his footing and spun around once, barely managing to grab hold of Keel in the process.
“Sword-bro, I’m falling!”
His eyes screamed I refuse to fall! as he glared daggers at me. Sorry about that. The scenario for how this act was supposed to go had already been decided, after all.
“I’m falling! I’m falling!”

Keel clung desperately to the rope, with Ren clinging just as desperately to Keel. According to Luna-chan, the sight of Ren struggling gamely to grab Keel’s hand and haul himself back onto the rope was apparently plucky and adorable.
“Kweh—!”
Below, Luna-chan waited, ever eager, for the moment to arrive.
“Heave-hooooo!”

With a valiant, never-say-die effort, Keel managed to hoist Ren up rather impressively — but alas, the “friendship saves the day” route wasn’t in the script, so before Keel could finish lifting him all the way, I closed in and kicked them both right off.
“Whoa! Gyaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
BANG! went the gong, and at that very instant smoke came billowing up from below as Luna-chan caught Keel and Ren and tucked them away safely into her feathers.
Ren and Keel thrashed about within Luna-chan’s feathers, but right on cue, Luna-chan let out a cry as if to declare herself thoroughly satisfied.
“Kweh—!”
“Today’s sacrificial Beastmen have become bird-feed, and the noble human has crossed the rope in full! Come now, let us revel in humanity’s triumph!”

At that, the audience erupted in a thunderous wave of applause. Luna-chan promptly hurried off toward the back of the circus grounds and released Keel and Ren there. As for me, I finished crossing the rope and struck a victory pose. The act starring Keel and Ren ended in a resounding success, indeed.
